PaidPadding uses this adapter and the prior paid-prefix/bit-plane composition. Its resources are53+Q+(M.k+extra)*max(1,M.g.size) tapes,5 symbols and cellBits=3. Given fixed rational maps F,any original payload M and eta>0,choose K and extra once before the dimension,input family and time coefficient. Assuming the overlap graphs have vertex expansion eta at the considered dimensions,each payload computation bounded by t is preserved with additive C*P time and zero-slack CutIneq at its actual halting time. For any dimension sequence tending to infinity and any task instances computed by M within a*P,uniform_linear_tasks_macrostar gives actual halting horizons at most(C+a)*P,correct outputs,the cut inequality,and NativeRunLimits.Conclusion for this same fixed machine. That conclusion explicitly includes uniformly convergent subsequences,every-subsequence1-Lipschitz limits,the full excised-label inequality,total excess>=1,range bound,and failure of simultaneous monotonicity. It reuses the first paper theoremMStar_walk; no limit proof was duplicated.

cleanup_inventory.finding: In progress. R1753 proves an exact cleanup inventory and a native eraser for bare nonblank streams. The generator has seven marked words, two lone START markers, four bare streams and 29 blank tapes. Their absolute head positions are now verified: marked words, lone markers and blank tapes have head zero; two streams start at zero and two end at their exact length. Every stream symbol is nonblank. The complete generated page schedule has zero net displacement, so all page heads and the clock head finish at zero. The page tapes and ten radius scratch tapes are already blank. NativeSpanErase physically erases an arbitrary nonblank span, including any START/STOP symbols as ordinary data, in at most 5m+4 steps from its left endpoint or 3m+3 from its right endpoint, restoring the left-end absolute position. Its fixed original-model machine has one tape, five symbols and seven states. Every step is paid; there is no implicit erasure or head reset. These facts prepare a concrete cleanup controller; they do not yet execute the complete cleanup.

generator_cleanup.finding: In progress. R1754 constructs and verifies the fixed generator cleanup machine:42 existing tapes,5 symbols,92 states,independent of the map family and input. It invokes the seven marked-word erasers,the two marker removals and four bare-stream erasers with every transfer paid. From the exact OpcodeGenerator endpoint it halts with every tape wholly blank and all42 absolute heads at zero,preserving input position and output. Its exact budget is the sum of marked-word and stream erasure costs plus paid transfers. For a canonical input of length P=inputLength(n),n>=1,and a dimension word of value n and length n.size,the total cost is at most C_F*P,where C_F depends only on the fixed rational map family. Stream lengths are bounded using previously proved paid generation traces; equal-length binary value uniqueness identifies their dimension words. Thus no uncharged length oracle or implicit erasure is used. This is a prepared-endpoint cleanup theorem,not yet the integrated blank-start paid prefix.

complete_cleanup.finding: In progress. R1755 discharges paid workspace cleanup through the complete native computation/cut/MStar chain. PaidCleanup combines the42-tape generator cleanup with physical radius-clock erasure on the existing53+Q tapes;it has5 symbols and100 states. Its initial tape contents and absolute heads match PaidReady.finalConfig exactly,and its cost is at most(GeneratorCleanup.coefficient(F)+28K+5)*P. PaidClean extends the actual blank-start prefix with this paid cleanup,preserves every original successful-prefix head position,and halts with every work cell blank,all work and input heads zero,and no output. It adds100 states and no tapes. Four existing PaidPayload modules were updated in place to use PaidClean. Their arbitrary-computation preservation,excursion layout,zero-slack CutIneq,and the existing PaidPadding fixed-parameter/MStar theorems now concern this same cleaned machine. execute_with_blank_prefix proves that every successful payload segment runs with the prefix bank frozen wholly blank and all its heads zero. The original201 sections8/12 cleanup obligation is therefore discharged; no duplicate parallel payload implementation was introduced.

all_size_expansion.finding: In progress. R1756 removes the even-dimension restriction at the same epsilon/2 vertex-expansion constant for every positive grid size, including size 1. HalfGridExpansion selects exactly n half-cells inside any coarse grid-cell union of measure at least 1/2; the resulting subset has measure exactly 1/2. Continuous expansion and image monotonicity give neighbor expansion capped at the real half-size. AllSizeOverlapExpansion converts the two-sided capped inequalities to ordinary vertex expansion. ContinuousNativePadding connects the resulting symmetric rational graph to the complete paid native arbitrary-computation, zero-slack CutIneq and MStar chain. The refinement is proof-only: the generated graph, machine, runtime bound and fixed parameter order are unchanged. Fixed rational continuous expanding-family existence remains an explicit premise.

source.finding: The actual construction uses fixed rational Mobius maps and inverses restricted to unit input/output intervals, rational translations and identity. Theorem1.2 is the continuous expansion obligation. Its proof uses a restricted spectral gap and deeper group-growth inputs; those are not provided by the native compiler. Targeted local Mathlib searches for the named inputs found no ready theorem. Do not treat citation as a kernel proof.

closed_unit_restrictions.finding: In progress. R1757 proves the exact rational unit-domain and measure adapters for the source expansion construction. RationalUnitMobius uses rational coefficients, positive determinant and six strict linear inequalities. Clipping computes lo=max(0,-b/a) and hi=min(1,(d-b)/(a-c)); the interval is nondegenerate and is exactly the closed set where input and output lie in [0,1]. The coefficient conditions are preserved by adjugate inversion, cover opposite translations and identity, and follow from coefficient deviations below 1/4 or squared sum below 1/16. The finite augmented source family is constructed and its image union decomposed exactly. For every finite rational map family and arbitrary input set, replacing closed domains by open domains removes only finitely many endpoint images, hence preserves outer measure and real measure exactly. Restricted source expansion therefore supplies the existing epsilon/2 all-size graph expansion and the same complete native arbitrary-computation, CutIneq and MStar conclusions. No analytic expansion or generator-existence claim is inferred from these adapters.

construction with input/output restrictions, inverses, translations and identity
Theorem 1.2 and its reduction to Theorem 1.3
source.finding: The source has closed interval domains; the graph compiler has open domains. Rational clipping with positive determinant and six strict linear inequalities gives the exact closed unit input/output restriction. These inequalities hold whenever all coefficient deviations from identity are below 1/4, in particular when their squared sum is below 1/16, and are stable under the adjugate inverse. A finite family loses at most two endpoint images per map on passing to the open domain. Spectral-gap and generator-existence proofs are not supplied by these algebraic and measure bridges.

translation_uniformity.finding: In progress. R1758 proves the first analytic reduction of continuous expansion for the actual augmented rational family. Its identity and legal opposite translations preserve the original set and shifted cell parts. The measure gain is at least the absolute difference of the occupied measures of two adjacent grid cells. The grid partition covers every unit-interval set up to a finite null boundary, and its cell masses sum exactly to the set measure. A finite path-and-average argument therefore proves that expansion at most 1+sigma implies |K*m_i-M| <= K*(K-1)*sigma*M for every cell, where M=volume(A), m_i=volume(A intersect cell_i), K>=2 and sigma>=0. An explicit expansion-or-uniformity dichotomy follows. No half-measure restriction is required for this intermediate reduction. The K*(K-1) factor is a routine sharpening of the source K^2 estimate, not a novelty claim or an unconditional expansion proof.

source.section: Proof of Theorem 1.2, translation reduction and equation (1.2)
source.scope: The actual augmented finite family is reused. The formal bound is K(K-1)*sigma*measure(A), slightly sharper than the source K^2 factor; no half-measure assumption is needed for this intermediate result. This is a formalized source reduction with a routine constant refinement, not a novelty claim.

trimming_projection_error.finding: In progress. R1759 discharges cell trimming and its actual squared-integral projection error. GridTrimming proves exact occupied mass sums for selected cells, the complementary mass partition, the changed occupancy of each retained/deleted cell, and a loss bound theta*(1+delta)*M from original normalized cell error delta. Removing the first and last m cells deletes exactly 2m cells and leaves a subset of [m/K,1-m/K], for 2m<=K. GridProjectionError constructs actual real step functions, proves their integrability and exact squared-integral formula, and proves the cell-centered indicator has zero integral on every cell. The difference between globally centered and cell-centered indicators equals a step function almost everywhere, with an integrable square. After trimming, its squared integral is at most ((delta+theta*(1+delta))^2+theta)*M^2, where theta is the removed-cell fraction. The final theta term explicitly charges zeroed cells. Source-family corollaries substitute delta=K*(K-1)*sigma and theta=2m/K. This is a proved error budget toward the analytic expansion theorem, not that theorem itself.

source.section: Proof of Theorem 1.2: boundary trimming and cell-mean projection
source.scope: Use the source strategy, but prove an explicit error formula for actual centered functions. If a fraction theta of cells is deleted and the original normalized cell error is delta, squared-integral centering error is at most ((delta+theta*(1+delta))^2+theta)*M^2. The theta term explicitly charges deleted cells. This supplies a needed proof obligation; it is not a claim that the published theorem is false or a novelty claim.

variance_normalized_spectral_input.finding: In progress. R1760 completes the normalized analytic input for the trimmed cell-centered function. CellCenteredVariance proves membership in every finite or infinite Lp exponent, exact squared integral M_prime-K*sum_i(m_i_prime^2), a lower bound from a cell-mass cap, and positive variance when 0<M<=1/2, 0<=delta<1 and theta*(1+delta)<1. It also proves the function vanishes outside the retained cells. If delta<=1/100 and theta<=1/200, its variance is at least (49/100)*M, and the squared-integral error from global centering is at most one hundredth of this variance. CellCenteredSpectralInput constructs the actual real L2 equivalence class, identifies its norm square with the variance integral, normalizes it, proves its representative has zero integral on every grid cell, and proves almost-everywhere support in the retained cells and hence the central interval for central trimming. The final spectral-input theorem identifies the normalized function explicitly with this trimmed indicator. These are formal analytic prerequisites; no spectral-gap or rational-generator-existence result is assumed or claimed.

source.section: Proof of Theorem 1.2: boundary trimming and cell-mean projection
source.scope: This supplies the variance and normalized L2 input in the source strategy, with explicit retained-cell support and a charged deleted-cell contribution. It does not supply the restricted spectral gap or generator existence and makes no novelty claim.

near_identity_mobius_calculus.finding: In progress. R1761 completes quantitative near-identity Mobius control and reuses Mathlib for actual change of variables. MobiusCalculus proves the derivative formula, its positivity and continuity, measurable images, the real image-measure integral formula, and the exact squared-integral identity for the square-root-Jacobian weighted pullback on measurable subsets of the existing rational interval. It proves both inverse compositions on the unit interval, the reciprocal derivative identity, and the unit-restricted preimage/inverse-image equality under its explicit domain hypothesis. NearIdentityMobius bounds coefficients entrywise by eta, transfers the condition to the adjugate inverse, and derives it from squared coefficient distance at most eta^2. For eta<=1/8 and x in [0,1], the denominator lies between 1-2eta and 1+2eta, displacement is at most 8eta, and derivative and square-root-derivative errors are at most 32eta. These imply actual image-measure distortion between factors 1-32eta and 1+32eta. A central interval [r,1-r] with r>=8eta lies in the clipped domain and maps into [0,1], for the map and its inverse. The corresponding preimage identity is proved. These local identities do not by themselves establish a unitary L2 representation, almost-invariance, the spectral gap, or generator existence.

source.section: Section 1, construction and proof of Theorem 1.2; operator preceding Theorem 1.3
source.scope: Source reread this turn. Use explicit entrywise error eta; the squared coefficient-distance hypothesis is bounded by eta^2. Prove actual derivatives, change of variables, adjugate inverse identities and weighted energy locally on the rational interval. Do not infer a full L2 unitary representation or the spectral gap from these local identities.

small_expansion_weighted_indicator.finding: In progress. R1762 converts small augmented-family expansion into actual unweighted and Jacobian-weighted indicator error. SmallExpansionSymmDiff proves a finite-measure common-cover inequality, inclusion of each generator/inverse image in the actual augmented cover, and the symmetric-difference bound B=2*sigma*M+2*(M-M_prime)+32*eta*M_prime for the centrally trimmed set T. It substitutes the existing trimming loss to give an explicit bound in sigma, delta, eta and m/K. IndicatorPullbackError proves the pointwise indicator/symmetric-difference identity, integrability of the square, and the exact unit-interval integral as the measure of the inverse-map image symmetric difference. Both generator and inverse corollaries are proved. WeightedIndicatorError proves measurability and a pointwise square-root-Jacobian error estimate, derives integrability of the actual weighted error before comparing integrals, and bounds its unit-interval energy by 2*(1+32*eta)*B+2*(32*eta)^2*M_prime. The central-trim corollary replaces B by C*M, where C=2*sigma+4*m/K*(1+delta)+32*eta, and M_prime by M. This proves almost-invariance of the uncentered trimmed indicator locally on [0,1]; global centering and the normalized spectral input remain separate obligations.

source.section: Proof of Theorem 1.2: near-invariance of the trimmed indicator before centering and projection
source.scope: The source was reread in R1761. This checkpoint supplies an explicit small-expansion error budget, including mass discarded by trimming and Jacobian distortion. The unweighted indicator energy is identified with a symmetric-difference measure. The weighted energy is proved integrable, then bounded for both each generator and its inverse. This is a local [0,1] statement for the uncentered indicator, not yet the normalized spectral input or a completed spectral-gap proof.

cell_centered_error_and_correlation.finding: In progress. R1763 completes centering, boundary and projection charges in the small-expansion argument. WeightedEnergyTransfer proves local squared-energy contraction for the actual Jacobian-weighted pullback, integrability and a general projection-transfer inequality. UnitBoundaryError confines points escaping [0,1] to two strips of total measure at most 16*eta, then bounds the weighted unit-indicator error. CellCenteredAlmostInvariant combines these with the trimmed-indicator and projection estimates to obtain the actual cell-centered error for both each generator and its inverse. CellCenteredRelativeError proves a concrete parameter budget, yielding weighted squared error at most V/16 and correlation at least 3*V/4, where V is the global squared integral of the actual cell-centered function. No spectral gap is assumed or proved in these estimates; they supply the lower-correlation side of the eventual contradiction.

source.scope: Quantitative centering/projection and almost-invariance support. Not a new restricted spectral-gap proof or global unitary representation.

conditional_spectral_expansion.finding: In progress. R1764 proves jointly feasible parameters and the conditional continuous-expansion theorem. ExpansionParameters chooses m=ceil(8*eta*K), sigma=1/(100*K^2), delta=K*(K-1)*sigma, and proves every numeric hypothesis for eta<=1/1000000 and K>=10000. Uniformity follows from actual small augmented expansion. NormalizedCellCorrelation supplies a measurable representative of the existing normalized L2 class, exact unit squared integral, unit support, zero integrals on both open and closed cells, and correlation at least 3/4. ConditionalSpectralExpansion proves integrability of weighted products, equality of the symmetric correlation average with the integral of the averaged weighted action, and the continuous expansion bound with margin sigma from the explicit RestrictedCorrelationGap premise. It handles null sets separately and derives positive variance for positive-measure sets. The bound transfers to the existing open-domain interface; an eventual-gap premise yields a fixed nonempty rational expanding family. Existence of RestrictedCorrelationGap is not asserted.

source.scope: Theorem 1.2 reduction and Theorem 1.3 statement. The function-form gap uses the actual weighted action, normalized squared integral, closed cell integrals and symmetric average. The normalized representative is proved equal almost everywhere to the prior L2 construction. No formal proof of the global SL2 unitary representation, restricted gap or generator existence is claimed.

global_real_mobius_representation.finding: In progress. R1765 formalizes the real fractional-linear action of actual SL(2,R) matrices. It proves inverse/product identities away from the pole, finite exceptional sets, measurability, positive Jacobian off the pole, and global change of variables and integrability equivalence. The weighted pullback W_g(f)(x)=|c*x+d|^(-1)*f((a*x+b)/(c*x+d)) preserves squared integrals and respects almost-everywhere equality. It descends to a linear isometric equivalence of the actual L2 quotient. T_g=W_(g inverse) is packaged as a group homomorphism into linear isometric equivalences, with norm, inverse, composition and inner-product laws proved. Determinant-one rational maps and their square-root-Jacobian action agree exactly with this global construction. Their finite symmetric average is a continuous linear contraction and is symmetric for the real inner product. The actual L2 restricted-gap premise implies the function-form premise from R1764, and hence the proved continuous expansion bound. Neither gap existence nor strong continuity in the matrix parameter is asserted.

source.scope: Theorem 1.3 global weighted representation and exact normalized L2 gap statement, including the inverse convention. The Jacobian theorem, matrix special linear group, Lp classes, continuous linear maps and linear isometry equivalences are reused from Mathlib. No restricted spectral gap is assumed implicitly or proved to exist.
source.section3_reread: R1765; claims 3.2–3.4 and the dependency on flattening Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.5

classical_grid_fourier_and_correlation.finding: In progress. R1766 proves cancellation against tests with bounded cell oscillation, the explicit classical Fourier estimate |Ff(xi)| <= (2*pi*|xi|/K)*||f||_1, and the unit-support inequality ||f||_1^2 <= integral ||f||^2. For normalized real L2 representatives supported in [0,1] with zero closed-grid-cell means, the classical low-frequency squared integral on [-R,R] is at most 8*pi^2*R^3/K^2. A threshold uniform over these functions makes this at most 1/256. Separately, every real Hilbert-space linear contraction satisfies |<Tf,f>-<Tg,g>| <= ||f-g||*(||f||+||g||). If ||f||=1, ||f-g||<=1/16 and <Tf,f>>=1/2, then <Tg,g>>=95/256. This applies to the actual Mobius average. The identification of the classical integral with Mathlib's L2 Fourier transform and the actual high-frequency decomposition are still unproved here.

source.scope: Quantitative ingredients of Claim 3.2: exact zero-cell-mean cancellation and correlation stability. The classical Fourier integral uses exp(-2*pi*i*x*frequency). Mathlib L2 Fourier is defined separately by extension from Schwartz maps; its agreement on L1 intersection L2 is not assumed. No novelty claimed for these standard analytical steps.

l2_fourier_bridge_and_high_frequency.finding: In progress. R1767 proves that the classical Fourier integral and Mathlib's L2 Fourier transform agree almost everywhere for every L1-intersection-L2 input, using equality against smooth compactly supported tests and the tempered-distribution compatibility theorem. Actual low/high-frequency L2 components are constructed, with exact Fourier representative formulas, norm contraction, and an exact low-component energy identity. Real and imaginary part maps reuse the existing real Mobius action: its complexification preserves contraction and symmetry, agrees with the real action on embedded real inputs, and each group action has the expected complex weighted-pullback formula almost everywhere. For a normalized unit-supported real L2 input with zero K-cell means, 2048*pi^2*R^3<=K^2 makes the low component norm <=1/16. If original average correlation is >=1/2, the complementary component g has norm <=1, no Fourier mass on [-R,R], distance <=1/16 from the original complexified input, and real-inner-product correlation >=95/256>1/4. This is an explicit sharp-cutoff high-frequency reduction; smooth Littlewood-Paley band isolation and the spectral-gap contradiction remain.

source.scope: The classical integral agrees almost everywhere with Mathlib L2 Fourier by smooth-test uniqueness and tempered-distribution compatibility. The new witness uses a sharp interval cutoff; source Claim 3.2 is stated for a Littlewood-Paley high-frequency sum. Smooth band decomposition and spatial-tail/derivative controls in Claim 3.3 remain, and no global smooth near-identity bound is inferred from matrix entrywise closeness. No novelty claimed for standard analytical support.

weighted_derivative_moments_and_regulari.finding: In progress. R1768 proves the exact differential expression D_g u(y)=(a-c*y)^2*u'(y)-c*(a-c*y)*u(y) for the weighted pullback W_g u(x)=|c*x+d|^(-1)*u((a*x+b)/(c*x+d)). Away from the possible pole, (W_g u)'=W_g(D_g u); the almost-everywhere identity gives exact derivative-energy transport. An explicit four-moment estimate is proved with coefficients 16*a^4, 16*c^4, 4*c^2*a^2 and 4*c^4. All even polynomial L2 moments of Schwartz inputs and their derivatives are integrable, and D_g preserves Schwartz space. Cubic decay proves derivative zero at the pole, closing the jump/singularity issue. Hence W_g u is globally C-infinity for every Schwartz input, its nth derivative is W_g(D_g^n u), and every derivative is in L2 with exact energy equality. The complex pullback is identified with the existing complexified actual group action using its inverse convention. Uniform scale-dependent moment bounds for actual smooth band pieces, band isolation and the restricted spectral gap remain.

source.reread: R1768 source opened; R1767 Section 3 Claims 3.2-3.4 inspection retained.
source.scope: Standard analytic support for source band localization. All spatial moments are explicit. Pole extension proved using cubic decay; no jump term hidden by almost-everywhere differentiation. Smoothness and finite moments do not assert uniform scale bounds for arbitrary translated band-limited functions. No novelty claimed.

l2_derivative_fourier_and_separated_corr.finding: In progress. R1769 proves integration by parts against Schwartz tests for functions and derivatives in L2 without an L1 assumption. A weak derivative represented by an L2 class gives the actual Fourier representative identity F(df)(xi)=2*pi*i*xi*F(f)(xi), exact derivative energy, and integrability of the weighted Fourier energy. The actual high-frequency component satisfies (2*pi*R)||P_high f||<=||df|| for R>=0 and the divided bound for R>0. These results are connected to the existing complexified Mobius action on Schwartz inputs, with null-set transport proved for arbitrary real normed target spaces. Iterated transported derivatives have the expected Fourier powers. The high-frequency energy is bounded by the four explicit spatial moments from R1768. Low-frequency orthogonality gives |<W_g u,h>_real|<=||D_g u||_2*||h||_2/(2*pi*R) whenever Fh vanishes on [-R,R]. Smooth band construction, square-summed moment estimates and band isolation remain.

source.scope: Standard Fourier/Sobolev support for the band localization step. Mathlib integration by parts for integrable products, L2 Fourier/Schwartz compatibility, and uniqueness against smooth compactly supported tests are reused. No L1 assumption on transformed functions and no claim that Mobius images remain Schwartz. The new separated-correlation estimate retains the actual transported derivative norm. Quantitative summability over bands is not proved.
source.next_route: Direct smooth frequency multipliers: Real.contDiff_fourier and Real.iteratedDeriv_fourier apply to unit-supported L1/L2 inputs; a smooth compact cutoff times their Fourier transform embeds in Schwartz space, and inverse Fourier preserves Schwartz. Prefer this to constructing a new mixed L1-L2 convolution library. The key remaining estimates are square sums over bands of normalized transported derivative energies, not a uniform band-by-band relative derivative bound.

actual_smooth_bands_and_spectrum_derivat.finding: In progress. R1770 proves that all polynomial moments x^n*f of a unit-supported L2 input are L1 and L2 with L2 norm at most ||f||. Its classical Fourier transform is smooth, every nth derivative is in L2, and the derivative energy is at most (2*pi)^(2n)*||f||^2. For every compactly supported Schwartz cutoff chi, chi*Ff is embedded in Schwartz space and its inverse Fourier transform is an actual Schwartz band. The band's L2 Fourier representative is exactly chi times the original L2 Fourier representative; exact energy, norm bounds and frequency-zero statements are proved. A pointwise weighted square-sum bound on cutoff values controls total band energy. First and second derivatives of the actual band spectrum satisfy explicit finite-family energy bounds in terms of square-sum constants B0,B1,B2 for cutoff values and derivatives. The constants do not depend on the number of bands. Concrete dyadic cutoffs, spatial-moment conversion, transported derivative square sums and band isolation remain.

source.scope: Standard analytic support for source Claim 3.3. Reuses Mathlib Real.contDiff_fourier, Real.iteratedDeriv_fourier, HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap, Schwartz/L2 Fourier compatibility and the iterated Leibniz rule. No novelty claimed. The original unit-supported input is retained in every moment estimate; no support assumption is transferred to its high-frequency truncation. Family size does not enter the energy constants, but explicit square-sum bounds on cutoffs and their derivatives are still hypotheses until the dyadic family is constructed.

exact_spatial_moments_and_transport_ener.finding: In progress. R1771 proves the exact Plancherel identity for every polynomial spatial moment of any complex Schwartz function, with no spatial support hypothesis. For each actual smooth band u=F_inverse(chi*Ff), its derivative is exactly the smooth band with cutoff q(xi)=2*pi*i*xi*chi(xi); q is compactly supported Schwartz. The R1770 finite-family frequency derivative estimates now give the spatial moments needed for D_g u=(a-c*x)^2*u'-c*(a-c*x)*u. Five explicit pointwise weighted square-sum bounds on chi, chi', q, q', q'' control the sum of ||D_g u_i||_2^2, with a displayed constant independent of family size. A finite-family high-frequency tail estimate permits different thresholds for different bands. Concrete dyadic cutoffs, their coefficient bounds, L2 decomposition and band isolation remain.
exact_spatial_moments_and_transport_ener.source: Local Mathlib Schwartz Fourier Plancherel and differentiation APIs; previous source context: Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, Section 3 Claims 3.2–3.4. No new external claim or novelty claim.

concrete_dyadic_coefficients_and_transpo.finding: In progress. R1772 constructs an actual compactly supported smooth cutoff rho, equal to one on [-1,1], zero outside [-2,2], and bounded in norm by one. Its dyadic differences chi_j=rho(xi/2^(j+1))-rho(xi/2^j) are actual compactly supported Schwartz functions, vanish at and outside the prescribed annular boundaries, and satisfy an exact finite telescoping identity. Closed dyadic annuli have overlap at most three, including boundary points needed for derivative supports. Exact dilation identities give uniform pointwise square-sum bounds for every derivative order of chi_j and q_j=i*2*pi*xi*chi_j with weights 2^(-2j). The five R1771 coefficient hypotheses are fully discharged. For the actual bands, total unweighted L2 energy and weighted transported derivative energy are uniformly bounded over every finite index set; an actual Fourier-tail bound with individual thresholds follows. L2 convergence of the telescoping band sums and band isolation remain.
concrete_dyadic_coefficients_and_transpo.source: Local Mathlib primary source: ContDiffBump.InnerProduct, SchwartzSpace.Basic/Deriv, IteratedDeriv.Lemmas, Deriv.Support, and dyadic powers/finite intervals. Standard analytical support; no novelty claimed. Earlier Bourgain–Yehudayoff Section 3 context is unchanged.

dyadic_L2_reconstruction_and_far_correla.finding: In progress. R1773 proves that the actual low-frequency Schwartz bands converge in L2 to the original unit-supported input, using an exact Fourier error identity and dominated convergence. The finite dyadic band sums telescope in Schwartz space and L2 and converge to h=F_inverse((1-rho)*Ff). This component has norm at most ||f||, Fourier transform zero on [-1,1], and distance from f bounded by its sharp [-2,2] low-frequency projection. For normalized real grid inputs with K^2>=16384*pi^2 and original average correlation at least 1/2, h is within 1/16, has correlation at least 95/256, and its finite band sums eventually have correlation at least 1/3. The actual band correlation at offset d has a summed bound proportional to 2^(-d). Summing offsets at least D gives an upper-triangular distant-band bound proportional to 2^(-D), uniform in both truncations. The symmetric average and band-isolation conclusion remain.
dyadic_L2_reconstruction_and_far_correla.source: Local Mathlib primary APIs for dominated convergence, continuous sqrt and inner products, L2 Fourier isometry, finite Cauchy–Schwarz and finite sums. Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, Section 3 Claims 3.2–3.4 (https://arxiv.org/html/1108.2555#S3) re-read in R1773. Claim 3.3 requires a uniform positive band norm ratio; universality is still to be proved when assembling bounded-matrix constants. No novelty claimed for standard analytical support.

uniform_dyadic_band_isolation.finding: In progress. R1774 assembles the exact symmetric complex average from the forward and inverse Mobius actions. The transport constant is bounded by one fixed constant when |g00| and |g10| are at most two; controlling |g11| also supplies the inverse bound. Thus upper and lower distant-band sums decay as 2^(-D) with a constant independent of the input, truncations, number of generators and generator choice within this bounded class. A finite symmetric-matrix reindexing and the shifted band-energy estimate control the near part. If every band has norm ratio at most r, the finite quadratic correlation is at most 2*(D*r*B0 + 2^(-D)*L)*||f||^2. Choosing universal D and r>0 makes this less than 1/3 for unit inputs. Hence a finite band sum with correlation at least 1/3 implies that the full decomposition has some nonzero band u_j with ||T u_j||>r*||u_j||; no bound j<N is asserted. The grid-input corollary uses the verified R1773 eventual finite correlation. This is currently a level-zero decomposition, not the arbitrary-high-start version needed later.
uniform_dyadic_band_isolation.source: Local Mathlib primary APIs for finite sums, finite injective reindexing, real inner products, powers and ordered-field estimates. Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, Section 3 Claims 3.3–3.4 and Proposition 3.5 (https://arxiv.org/html/1108.2555#S3) re-read in R1774. The current actual-band isolation starts at level zero; arbitrary high starting level and normalized selected-band quantitative regularity remain. No novelty claimed for this analytical support.

joint_high_band_regularity_selection.finding: In progress. R1775 extends actual dyadic reconstruction to every starting level J and proves the corresponding grid correlation estimate under K^2>=16384*pi^2*2^(3J). A reusable finite correlation lemma and arbitrary band masks extend the universal norm-ratio theorem to any retained family; the old level-zero proof now reuses this more general result. Finite sums of actual bands satisfy ||sum u_j||^2<=3*sum||u_j||^2 by their bounded Fourier overlap. A concrete nonnegative regularity cost M_j, combining ||u_j||^2, ||x*u_j||^2 and 2^(-2j)*(||u_j'||^2+||x^2*u_j'||^2), has a fixed summed bound C*||f||^2. Discarding bands with M_j>R*||u_j||^2 for the fixed R=3*1024^2*(C+1) costs at most 1/1024 in L2 for every finite subfamily of a unit input. The retained sums preserve sufficient correlation, so a band j>=J is selected with u_j!=0, ||T u_j||>r*||u_j|| and M_j<=R*||u_j||^2, simultaneously. Both r and R are independent of J, the input, the grid and the bounded generator family.

group_action_continuity_smoothing.finding: In progress. Finite Borel measures give integrable actual representation orbits T_g=W_(g^-1). Their Bochner averages contract for probability measures and satisfy the exact convolution identity A_(mu*nu)=A_mu o A_nu. Consequently right-convolution smoothing changes A_mu u by at most ||A_nu u-u||, and by at most 29*2^j*sqrt(R)*eta for a kernel nu supported almost everywhere in the stated near-identity entry neighborhood. The error is independent of mu's support size or word length. A corresponding half-norm lower bound is proved whenever the error is at most half a known original lower bound.

generator_walk_haar_smoothing.finding: In progress. column_haar_polar_box_geometry.finding: In progress. R1781 constructs global column/shear coordinates for SL2: for v nonzero and q=v0^2+v1^2, the second column is (-v1,v0)/q+b*v. Reconstruction is exact. Left multiplication acts by the determinant-one linear map on v and a measurable fiberwise translation on b, so the pushforward mu0 of Lebesgue dv db is left invariant. The zero-column fiber is null; the inverse coordinates are continuous, map mu0 back to Lebesgue measure, and prove finiteness on compact sets. Mu0 is a nonzero Haar measure and the already-used Haar measure H equals c_H*mu0 for a proved positive finite scalar. Polar change of variables gives density c_H*a da dtheta db on a>0, -pi<theta<pi, with the exact factorization into rotation and affineWaveletMatrix(a^2,a^2*b). Bounded entries imply a^2<=2B^2 and |b|<=B^2; the entry box is compact and H(box_B)<=8*c_H*B^4 for B>=0.

actual_walk_nonconcentration_and_initial.finding: In progress. R1788 establishes nonconcentration at the rational separation scale for the actual symmetric generator walk. The original action satisfies norm(A_mu f)^(2*2^k)<=norm(A_(alpha^(2^k))f) for unit f. Matrix-entry support and the existing coefficient estimate yield an explicit power bound. For every fixed k, sufficient flatness rho_k<=D with D^2<=2^j in the stated logarithmic walk-length window implies the required restricted quadratic-form gap. No comparison back to the original one-sided density is a premise of this reduction. The flatness premise itself, full product growth/metric BSG and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
restricted_gap_from_symmetric_iterates.source: This turn reuses the already proved Haar coefficient estimate, actual smoothed high-band witness, symmetric-power norm inequality and scalar dyadic barrier, together with the R1790 autocorrelation identities. It proves a new analytic interface to the intended Bourgain–Yehudayoff flattening program, not a new flattening theorem or a novel transposition lower bound. The canonical symmetric iterates are identified with actual convolution powers, including their mass, support, operator action and inherited initial bounds. Flatness of a fixed iterate remains an explicit premise of the final restricted-gap theorem. No source theorem is assumed as an axiom.

nonflattening_level_pair.finding: In progress. R1792 proves that a bounded nonnegative subprobability density whose self-convolution has squared L2 mass at least tau>0 contains a pair of dyadic level sets with quantitatively large weighted Haar multiplicative energy. The low tail costs at most8a in squared energy, with factor2 on the high part, without a finite-volume support hypothesis. Choosing a=tau/16 yields at most1+log2(max(1,16C/tau)) levels and a fourth-power loss in their number. The theorem is instantiated for the actual symmetric smoothed-autocorrelation iterate rho_k when integral rho_(k+1)^2>=tau; measurability, inverse symmetry and weighted level masses are included. Relative-energy normalization, self-energy conversion, metric BSG, SL2 product growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
nonflattening_level_pair.source: This formalizes the continuous dyadic-level extraction step in the Bourgain–Yehudayoff Monotone expansion flattening strategy (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, proof of Lemma4.1, equations4.3–4.5). The extraction is proved directly for Haar integrals, with explicit constants and a support-volume-free low-tail estimate, and applied to the actual R1791 symmetric autocorrelation densities. No novelty claim is made for these analytic support lemmas. The reference is motivation, not an axiom. No exact finite-group energy or metric discretization is silently substituted for continuous energy. Normalizing mixed energy, self-energy conversion, metric BSG and SL2 product growth/escape remain open formalization obligations.

nonflattening_self_energy.finding: In progress. R1793 upgrades the weighted level-pair extraction to relative Haar energy and then to one symmetric positive finite-volume level set with high self-energy. If f is a bounded symmetric probability density, U=integral f^2 and integral(f*f)^2>=theta*U for theta>0, there are N logarithmically bounded levels and one level A such that, for K=64N^4, theta/(K U)<=H(A)<=K/(theta U) and E(A,A)>=theta^2*H(A)^3/K^2. Positivity/finiteness of U and level volumes, noncommutative trace/Cauchy–Schwarz and every cancellation are checked. The result applies to the actual smoothed-autocorrelation iterates. Open/precompact regularization, continuous BSG, metric transfer, SL2 product growth/escape and strict flattening remain unproved; unconditional paid padding is incomplete.
nonflattening_self_energy.source: R1793 formalizes the continuous moment normalization and mixed-to-self energy part of the Bourgain–Yehudayoff Monotone expansion flattening strategy (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, proof of Lemma4.1, equations4.3–4.5). The proof uses the checked R1792 dyadic extraction, direct Haar convolution mass/pointwise bounds, an explicitly proved noncommutative trace identity and Cauchy–Schwarz. Every positivity, finiteness, symmetry and cancellation condition is proved or explicit. The returned level has a two-sided volume window and high self-energy. These are analytic support formalizations, not a new impossibility result or a novelty claim. Metric BSG, bounded-representative/covering details and SL2 product growth/escape remain unproved. No source theorem is assumed as an axiom. Fresh primary-source check: Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv math/0601431v3, Definition2.1 and Theorem5.4, supplies a continuous BSG target before the metric-entropy stage. Its multiplicative sets are nonempty open precompact sets. Our level sets are not yet proved to meet that topological hypothesis. The next bridge must establish it, rather than apply the source theorem to merely measurable sets.

open_energy_regularization.finding: In progress. R1794 closes the topological input gap between the measurable high-energy level and a symmetric nonempty open precompact set. Null-set support restriction preserves volume and energy. For every 0<delta<=1, outer regularity gives O with v<=H(O)<=(1+delta)v and compact closure inside Box(R+1), where R=(4B^2)^(2^k) comes from the base smoothed support Box(B). For K=64N^4, the actual nonflattening iterate gives theta<=K U H(O), theta U H(O)<=2K, and theta^2 H(O)^3<=8K^2 E(O,O), retaining the logarithmic bound on N. Continuous BSG, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
open_energy_regularization.source: R1794 directly proves the topological input bridge for the continuous Haar-energy route. Primary source rechecked: Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv math/0601431v3, Definition2.1 and Section5 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601431). The construction uses proved a.e. convolution invariance, outer regularity and existing compact entry boxes; no source theorem is assumed. It produces the nonempty open precompact input with explicit volume/energy/location bounds and arbitrarily small added volume. Continuous BSG itself remains unproved. These are supporting formalizations, not new impossibility theorems or novelty claims.

popular_product_relation.finding: In progress. R1795 proves that an open set O of finite positive Haar volume w, bounded in Box(Q), with E(O,O)>=w^3/L for positive finite L, has the explicit popular-product region C={1_O*1_O>w/(2L)}. It is nonempty open precompact, its closure lies in Box(2Q^2), H(C)<=2Lw, and the actual pairs in O x O with product in C have measure at least w^2/(2L). Lower semicontinuity follows directly from Fatou; product mass equals pair measure by a proved convolution-of-restrictions identity. The actual smoothed nonflattening iterates give this relation with L=8(64N^4)^2/theta^2 and prove L>=1 and finite, preserving the dyadic level, volume window and arbitrary small enlargement error. Weak BSG selection, small-product/approximate-group extraction, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
popular_product_relation.source: R1795 formalizes the self-energy popular-product step of Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv math/0601431v3, proof of Theorem5.2, equations18-19 and the following product-mass identity (https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601431). Rechecked the primary source and Lemma5.1 for the next selection target. The proof here directly uses Fatou, Haar convolution identities, Markov and elementary energy splitting. It derives the openness, bounded support and exact pair-measure identity rather than assuming them. The actual smoothed-iterate application is checked. This is a supporting formalization, not a new impossibility theorem or novelty claim. Weak BSG, approximate-group extraction, product growth/escape and strict flattening remain unproved.

weak_bsg_selection.finding: In progress. R1796 proves continuous weak-BSG selection. From product-pair measure at least H(A)H(B)/K it selects an actual fiber S={a in A:ab in C} with H(S)>H(A)/(2K), and a global popular quotient region D. Fewer than epsilon H(S)^2 pairs in S x S have aa'^-1 outside D, and epsilon H(B)H(D)<=2K^2 H(C)^2. S,D are nonempty open precompact for the bounded open SL2 inputs, with explicit entry bounds. A checked self-energy corollary gives S subset O with H(S)>H(O)/(4L), H(D)<=32L^4 H(O)/epsilon, the same exceptional-pair bound, and closure bounds Box(Q), Box(8Q^4). This closes the full simultaneous selection target, not just its moment bookkeeping. Full small-product BSG, approximate-group extraction, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
weak_bsg_selection.source: R1796 formalizes continuous weak-BSG selection following the mechanism of Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv math/0601431v3, Lemma5.1 (primary source read in R1795; https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601431). The new proof directly derives simultaneous size and low-codegree control using Cauchy–Schwarz, Tonelli and a positive finite weighted-averaging margin. It uses the relaxed size H(S)>H(A)/(2K), with strict exceptional-pair bound, and defines D as a global popular quotient region to reuse R1795 topology and Markov bounds. Its support and volume are quantitative. The self-energy corollary supplies H(S)>H(O)/(4L), H(D)<=32L^4 H(O)/epsilon and explicit entry boxes. These are supporting formalizations of a known mechanism, not novelty claims or new impossibility theorems. Full small-product BSG, approximate-group extraction, growth/escape and strict flattening remain unproved.

small_product_bsg.finding: In progress. R1797 proves full continuous small-product BSG for the self-energy input. If O is open in SL2(R), O subset Box(Q), w=H(O)>0, 1<=L<infinity and w^3<=L E(O,O), there exist open positive-volume A,B subset O with H(A)>=w/(64L^2), H(B)>=w/(8L), and H(AB)<=2^23 L^9 w. Their closures are compact in Box(Q), and closure(AB) is compact in Box(2Q^2). The proof constructs high-degree rows, applies the earlier weak-BSG selection, trims through strict good-degree superlevels, and proves a representation bound for EVERY selected product. This completes the R1796 next target. It is a supporting formalization of a known BSG argument with conservative constants, not a new transposition bound. Approximate-group extraction, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved.
small_product_bsg.source: Adaptation of Terence Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv:math/0601431v3, Theorem 5.2 (read again R1797); https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601431v3. Self-energy specialization with deliberately relaxed constants: row volume loss L^2 and product volume loss 2^23 L^9. This does not reproduce the source's sharper L^8 bound. Strict superlevels of good degree justify openness. Source Theorem 4.6 and Proposition 4.5 were also read for the next approximate-group extraction target. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds or novelty claims.

symmetric_core.finding: In progress. R1798 proves the continuous Ruzsa bound, inverse-energy trace identity, popular-overlap volume bounds, and a concrete symmetric open core T. For open A subset Box(Q), H(A)>0, finite K>=1 and H(AA^-1)<=K H(A), T={x:(1_(A^-1)*1_A)(x)>H(A)/(2K)} contains1, is inversion-symmetric and open, and has compact closure in Box(2Q^2). H(A)<=2K H(T)<=4K^2 H(A); for every n>=0, H(A*T^n*A^-1)<=2^n K^(2n+1)H(A). Hence H(A*T)<=2K^3 H(A) and H(T^3)<=16K^8 H(T). A direct composition from the R1797 self-energy input constructs A subset O and this T with K=2^55 L^21, H(O)<=2^62 L^23 H(T), and H(T)<=2^56 L^21 H(O). This completes the actual symmetric-core construction, including the representation proof for every sandwich power. Finite approximate-group covering, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds.
symmetric_core.source: Terence Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv:math/0601431v3, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601431v3. This turn implements the continuous Ruzsa specialization and the trace/popular-overlap argument of Lemma4.3 and Proposition4.5. All n sandwich powers were proved by a short convolution induction rather than separate n=1,n=3 proofs. The resulting constants match the displayed Proposition4.5 inequality; composition with the earlier deliberately relaxed self-energy BSG gives K=2^55 L^21. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new impossibility results. For the next step, Lemma3.6, Definition3.8 and Theorem3.10 were read R1798: the finite symmetric covering set must be contained in H^2. Plan H=T^3, using the proved n=7 sandwich bound and finite packing; do not substitute a weaker definition silently.

approximate_group_extraction.finding: In progress. R1799 proves a continuous finite-packing covering lemma, constructs U=T^3 with a finite symmetric doubling witness Y subset U^2, and composes this with actual self-energy extraction. For open O subset Box(Q), w=H(O)>0, finite L>=1 and w^3<=L E(O,O), put K=2^55 L^21. There are open positive-finite-volume A subset O and U containing1, with U inversion-symmetric and compact closure in Box(32Q^6), finite Y,W and x in W subset A subset O. One has card(Y)<=512K^16, U^2 subset Y*U, Y^-1=Y, A subset W*U, card(W)<=4K^4, w<=128K L^2 H(U), H(U)<=8K^7 w, and w<=256L^2K^4 H(O intersect x*U). The code reuses mathlib IsApproximateSubgroup and separately retains the stronger symmetric witness inside U^2. The finite covers and selected overlap are constructed, not assumed. Transfer to the original density level, metric transfer, SL2 growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds.
approximate_group_extraction.source: Terence Tao, Product set estimates for non-commutative groups, arXiv:math/0601431v3, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0601431v3, Lemma3.6, Definition3.8 and Theorem3.10 (read R1798). R1799 proves the continuous finite-packing cover, constructs U=T^3 using the R1798 n=7 bound, and retains an actual symmetric Y subset U^2. It reuses Mathlib.Combinatorics.Additive.ApproximateSubgroup.IsApproximateSubgroup rather than introducing a duplicate predicate. That library predicate does not require symmetry/containment of its finite witness, so these stronger source conditions are separately proved and returned. The existing finite-set small-tripling theorem does not apply to our continuous positive-Haar-volume sets; the continuous covering proof is supplied. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new impossibility theorems.

original_density_concentration.finding: In progress. R1800 removes the regularization-overlap gap: a measurable symmetric level with essentially bounded support and high self-energy yields an actual approximate group whose translate overlaps the ORIGINAL level. The regularization error is chosen after the level's loss parameter, with an exact half-budget absorption. Composition with actual smoothed autocorrelation nonflattening gives U, finite symmetric Y subset U^2 and x, all with explicit entry bounds, volume bounds and a positive probability bound for x*U under H.withDensity(rho_k). The logarithmic dyadic-level count is retained. No small-ball thickness or scale-sensitive cover is assumed. The original-density concentration target is complete; smoothing-scale local overlap and finite covering, product growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds.
original_density_concentration.source: R1800 preserves original measurable-level overlap through an explicit regularization budget, then composes with the actual smoothed autocorrelation nonflattening theorem. This is supporting formalization, not a new impossibility theorem. Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, Section4.1, equations4.11–4.12 and Theorem4.4 rechecked R1800: after approximate-group concentration, the source obtains local small-ball overlap and a scale-sensitive covering bound before invoking product growth. The source product theorem requires intermediate size, multiscale distribution and quantitative escape; finite covering alone does not prove flattening. Our conservative explicit constants and actual autocorrelation densities remain in force.

smoothing_scale_cover.finding: In progress. R1801 proves that every actual autocorrelation iterate retains a rightmost original smoothing kernel. A Haar averaging identity yields a concrete local-volume intersection from positive smoothed probability. Finite packing and explicit SL2 geometry then construct F subset U with U subset F*Ball(64Q^2 eta) and card(F)*p*H(Ball(eta))<=2cH(U), where U subset Box(Q), U^2 subset Y*U and card(Y)<=c. Composing with actual nonflattening concentration preserves all R1800 witnesses and yields card(F)*q^2*H(Ball(eta))<=2^23 K0 L^2K^20 H(U), with Q=32(R+1)^6. No uniform thickness, packing witness or local intersection is assumed. The finite cover is proved at its stated distorted radius; ordinary Frobenius eta-covering, product growth/escape, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds.
smoothing_scale_cover.source: R1801 formalizes the smoothing/local-overlap/finite-packing bridge corresponding to Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, Section4.1, equations4.11–4.12 (read R1800). The endpoint factorization is proved for the actual autocorrelation iterates and does not commute noncommuting factors or require inversion invariance of the kernel. The output is an actual finite cover by left translates of the identity ball of radius64Q^2 eta; the radius contains bounded-entry distortion. It is not yet an ordinary Frobenius eta-cover or a product-growth theorem. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new impossibility results.

frobenius_scale_covers.finding: In progress. R1802 refines the actual smoothing-scale cover to finite ordinary Frobenius eta-covers of U and U^6. Representatives belong to their respective target sets. The refinement costs at most 1025^4 Q^12 for U and (2^21+1)^4 Q^52 times card(Y)^5 for U^6. Composing with actual nonflattening retains the original geometry, volume and probability conclusions and gives card(E)*q^2*v_eta <= ofReal(1025^4 Q^12)*2^23 K0 L^2 K^20 H(U), and card(E6)*q^2*v_eta <= ofReal((2^21+1)^4 Q^52)*2^68 K0 L^2 K^100 H(U). Here v_eta=H(Ball(eta)). These explicit Q losses introduce no additional explicit inverse-eta power, but Q may itself depend on scale. Near-identity localization, product growth/escape, strict flattening, unconditional gap and paid padding remain unproved. These are supporting formalizations of known arguments, not new transposition bounds.
frobenius_scale_covers.source: R1802 supplies explicit ordinary Frobenius eta-covers for the nonflattening approximate group U and U^6, following the bounded-coordinate refinement and approximate-group covering route used with Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, Section 4.1 and Theorem 4.4 (read R1800). It preserves the Haar-ball scale factor and records all polynomial Q losses. This is supporting formalization of known arguments, not a new impossibility theorem. Product growth and its application remain unproved.

localized_cube_cover.finding: In progress. R1803 localizes A=U^2 intersect Ball(alpha), 0<alpha<=1. It proves that A is open, symmetric, contains1, has compact closure in Box(2), positive finite Haar volume and A^3 subset U^6. An actual finite translate cover proves H(U)<=M H(A), M=ofReal(33^4 Q^8/alpha^4), while H(A)<=512K^16 H(U). Every ordinary Frobenius eta-cover F of A, with arbitrary real 2x2 matrix centers, satisfies H(A)<=393216^4 card(F) v_eta when 0<eta<=1/32. The actual nonflattening composition retains all original geometry, volume and probability conclusions and the absolute E6 cardinality bound, and yields card(E6)*q^2<=D card(F) for EVERY such F, where E6 externally eta-covers A^3 and D=393216^4 ofReal((2^21+1)^4 Q^52) 2^68 K0 L^2 K^100 M. Native covering-number conversion, intermediate size, multiscale distribution, quantitative escape, product growth, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved. Supporting formalizations of known analysis, not new transposition bounds.
localized_cube_cover.source: R1803 proves quantitative near-identity localization and the finite-cover analogue of the small-tripling comparison used in Bourgain–Yehudayoff, Monotone expansion, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1108.2555, Section4.1/Theorem4.4, re-read this turn. Our explicit A=U^2 intersect Ball(alpha) differs from their quotient-set construction, so multiscale distribution and escape must be proved for this actual A; they are not inherited from a name or analogy. The product theorem, its premises, and strict flattening remain unproved. Supporting known-analysis formalization, not a new impossibility result.

native_frobenius_profile.finding: In progress. R1804 uses Mathlib's exact Frobenius metric and native external covering numbers. It proves the distance/squared-entry identity, finite attainment of external covering numbers, and a closed-to-strict radius-eta cover refinement of cost6561. Applied to the actual localized set A, it gives native covering numbers nA,n3 with0<nA<=n3<infinity, n3*q^2<=6561D*nA, q<=128*6561*393216^4*K0*K*L^2*M*V*nA*v_eta, and nA*q^3*V*v_eta<=A6*2^72*K0^2*L^2*K^107. The actual squared-L2 mass V is proved positive and finite, and the original geometry, probability concentration and volume comparisons remain in the same theorem. Absorbing the explicit losses into scale exponents, intermediate-size power bounds, multiscale distribution, quantitative escape, product growth itself, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain unproved. Supporting formalization, not a new transposition bound.
native_frobenius_profile.source: R1804 uses native Mathlib Matrix.Norms.Frobenius, Metric.externalCoveringNumber, IsCover, and ENat.toENNReal. The actual distance squared is proved equal to the sum of four squared entry differences. Closed radius-eta covers refine to strict radius-eta covers at cost6561, so the convention change is proved rather than assumed. A missing finite external-cover attainment lemma reuses the existing ENat infimum and definition. The actual nonflattening composition now has native positive finite covering numbers, a small-tripling bound and two-sided quantitative size control. This supports the Bourgain–Yehudayoff product-growth route previously audited, but does not yet absorb losses into scale exponents, prove multiscale distribution/escape, or prove the product theorem.

uniform_covering_interval.finding: In progress. R1805 absorbs all explicit nonflattening losses, the logarithmic level count, and the actual Haar normalization into a common power h^30000. With h=eta^-s and suitable positive s, one uniform small-scale threshold gives eta^(-kappa/2)<=N_eta(A)<=eta^(-3+gamma/2) and N_eta(A^3)<=eta^-beta*N_eta(A) for the actual localized witness A=U^2 intersect Ball(alpha). The theorem retains all previous geometry, approximate-group, probability-concentration, and quantitative volume/cover outputs. It derives these inequalities from the initial density cap, a lower squared-L2 mass bound, nonflattening, and the explicit support condition Q<=eta^-s; it does not assume the desired covering-number interval. Actual-walk support specialization, multiscale distribution, escape, product growth, strict flattening, and unconditional paid padding remain. Supporting formalization, not a new transposition bound.
uniform_covering_interval.source: R1805 reuses native Mathlib logarithm/rpow asymptotics, ENNReal finite-to-real conversion, actual Haar normalization, and the R1804 native closed Frobenius external-covering profile. All explicit coefficients are bounded by a common power without optimizing fixed constants. A uniform threshold is chosen before the measure, iterate, scale, and witness. The actual existence theorem retains all previous witness conclusions and adds the required intermediate-size and tripling powers. The actual support-growth specialization and the product-growth theorem remain unproved. This is supporting formalization of the existing route, not a new transposition lower bound.

actual_walk_covering_interval.finding: In progress. R1806 proves the covering-number interval and small-tripling bound for a fixed rational free family at each dyadic generator radius, for every admissible walk length and every bounded iterate. The previous support-growth and initial-density assumptions are derived from the actual walk. Only the lower energy threshold and nonflattening remain as analytic premises. The positive loss exponent is chosen BEFORE the maximum iterate; support/scale thresholds follow that iterate; the family is fixed before the smoothing scale and walk length. The conditional restricted-gap theorem now accepts any prescribed lower bound on the walk-selection constant, and the unchanged old statement reuses the strengthened proof. Distribution, escape, product growth, strict flattening, and unconditional paid padding remain. Supporting formalization, not a new transposition bound.
actual_walk_covering_interval.source: The actual rational walk now supplies the support-growth and initial-density conditions in the uniform covering interval, simultaneously for every iterate up to a fixed bound. Existing native support, initial free-family construction, logarithmic band-length regime, and covering profile are reused. The conditional spectral-gap theorem is strengthened to accept any prescribed lower bound Nmin, and the original theorem reuses it. Its original statement is byte-identical. No product-growth, escape, distribution or flatness premise is disguised as a proved fact. The positive loss exponent is chosen before the maximum iterate, which precedes the walk-selection bound and scale thresholds. This order is explicit in the final theorem statement.

localized_shortwalk_mass.finding: In progress. R1807 transfers the actual autocorrelation iterate's probability concentration to the localized set A=U^2 intersect Ball(alpha). For every t<=ell, the same A has a translate with quantitative mass under the actual t-step walk followed by the original smoothing kernel. The translating element has an explicit entry bound. The proof factors the actual iterate into a supported probability prefix and the shorter terminal smoothed walk, without commuting factors. The fixed rational family theorem retains every previous size, tripling, geometric, and probability output and its order of choices. Multiscale separated subsets, escape, product growth, strict flattening, and unconditional paid padding remain. Supporting formalization, not a new transposition bound.
localized_shortwalk_mass.source: R1807 reuses the existing finite-cover maximum, near-identity translate cover, actual convolution-power identity, and native probability convolution/lintegral operations. It proves actual mass localization and an exact shorter terminal-walk factor with a controlled prefix support, then composes both with the fixed free-family covering witness. No kernel/walk commutation or supremum attainment is assumed. The source product theorem (Bourgain–Yehudayoff, arXiv1108.2555, Theorem4.4 and Section4.1, reread this turn) requires separated subsets at intermediate scales, as well as a separate escape condition; neither is claimed proved here.

actual_dyadic_separated_subsets.finding: In progress. R1808 proves separated finite subsets inside the actual localized set at all dyadic scales rho=(1/4)^v with7680r<=v<=j, for smoothing eta=(1/4)^j and the existing logarithmic walk-length condition. The native ambient Frobenius separation is strict. The explicit bound is c<=4*C*M*|F|*rho^(1/30720), where c<=C times the actual iterate mass on xU and M=ofReal(33^4Q^8/alpha^4). The short length initialWalkLength(r,v)<=ell is derived. Freezing one common right-smoothing element cancels the large left translation in pairwise quotients and avoids any additive smoothing error or scale cutoff. The coefficient cost for the actual profile is proved <=h^1140 after dividing by q^2. Absorbing that loss, extending to all radii, and preserving the full family quantifiers still need composition. Escape, product growth, strict flattening and unconditional paid padding remain. No new transposition bound.
actual_dyadic_separated_subsets.source: R1808 proves a stronger extraction than the proposed additive-error route: select one common right-smoothing element by probability averaging, then cancel the common left translation in pairwise quotients. Frobenius submultiplicativity and the already proved rational denominator separation give separation with no additive smoothing error and no translating-element bound. Existing finite generator definitions, free-walk atom decay, initialWalkLength scale estimates and log-length compatibility are reused. The conclusion is a finite subset of the SAME localized set; no cover surrogate or product-theorem hypothesis is assumed. The complete all-radii power-law distribution statement, escape, product growth and flatness remain open.

uniform_all_radii_distribution.finding: In progress. R1809 proves that the same actual localized witness has, for EVERY real eta<rho<eta^epsilon, a finite subset F with strict ambient Frobenius separation>rho and |F|>=rho^(-1/122880). All previous covering, small-tripling, geometry, and every-short-walk concentration outputs are retained. The explicit h^1140 coefficient loss is absorbed, dyadic interpolation is proved, and the fixed scale cutoffs are derived. The small positive loss exponent s is chosen before the maximum iterate k; the rational free family is fixed before all later scales and walks. Only the existing energy threshold and nonflattening remain analytic premises. The distribution obligation is complete. Quantitative escape, product growth, strict flattening, unconditional gap and paid padding remain. No new transposition bound.
uniform_all_radii_distribution.source: R1809 composes the R1808 actual dyadic finite subsets and coefficient budget into the pure power-law distribution statement for every real eta<rho<eta^epsilon. Native geometric-scale interpolation, real powers and ENNReal.toReal operations are reused. The same actual witness retains all covering/tripling and short-walk mass outputs. The positive loss exponent precedes the maximum iterate and generator family; a radius-dependent scale cutoff is fixed before later inputs. Bourgain–Yehudayoff arXiv1108.2555 Theorem4.4 and Section4.1 were reread: this matches the form of the distribution assumption. Their independent complex-basis escape condition and the product theorem itself are not assumed or claimed proved.

actual_normalized_short_words.finding: In progress. R1810 strengthens actual smoothed-walk extraction to retain a nonempty finite set of free words of length<=t, denominator D^t, and one common smoothing element. Normalization at one endpoint preserves cardinality, includes the identity, doubles word length/denominator exponent, and puts a common conjugate inside A^-1*A. For the actual symmetric localized witness this is A^2, for every short length t<=ell. Under the already specified actual profile budgets, the dyadic initial length yields at least eta^(-1/122880) such distinct normalized words.
